result:
Your best growth channel is the 140 people who already pay you. In a 3 km delivery zone, word of mouth and visibility on your own streets will do more than ads, and they fit a €300/month budget. Here's what I'd do, roughly in priority order.

## 1. Launch gift subscriptions now
It's mid-November, so this is the most time-sensitive item. Sell 4-, 8- and 12-week gift boxes (€72 / €144 / €216) with a nice printed card. Many gift recipients will be nearby, because people buy for parents and neighbours, so they fall inside your zone. When a gift runs out, offer to convert it at the normal price; some will stay on. Promote it in the shop, in this week's boxes and on Instagram. Cost: printing only.

## 2. Start a referral programme
- **Offer:** "Give a friend their first box free, and get a free week yourself when they stay for a second box." Requiring the second box keeps people from signing up just for the freebie.
- **Cost:** about €18 of retail value per new customer, much less at ingredient cost. That's cheap when one subscriber is worth about €78 a month.
- **Make it physical:** put two "free first box" cards in every Saturday delivery. Most subscribers won't think to share a link, but they will hand a card to a neighbour.

## 3. Grow street by street
Cargo-bike delivery gets cheaper the more boxes you drop on one street. Map your current subscribers and pick the 3–4 streets or blocks with the most.
- Put leaflets through doors there, mentioning a neighbour: "12 households on your street already get Saturday bread from us."
- Ask whether a building or office could take a group drop-off.

Leafleting a few hundred homes costs €50–80 in printing and an afternoon of your time.

## 4. Offer a trial
"Try one box, no commitment, €12." Signing up for a weekly subscription is a big step, and a trial lowers it. Then email or message trial customers before the next Saturday to convert them. Track how many convert. If it's above 30–40%, put more of your budget into trials.

## 5. Partner with local businesses
Find 2–3 nearby shops that don't compete with you, such as a cheese shop, greengrocer, coffee roaster or wine shop.
- **Co-branded box:** the partner adds an item and both of you promote it to your customers.
- **Pickup points:** these let you reach people just outside your 3 km zone without longer bike routes.

## 6. Use the shop and Google
- **In the shop:** walk-in customers are your warmest leads. Add a visible sign at the till ("Get this every Saturday at your door, €18") and train the team to mention it.
- **Google Business Profile:** keep it current, add photos of the box, and ask happy subscribers for reviews. People search "sourdough near me."

## Suggested monthly €300 split
| Item | € |
|---|---|
| Referral and trial cards, leaflets | 80 |
| Free first boxes / referral rewards (at cost) | 120 |
| Gift cards and packaging (Nov–Dec) | 50 |
| Small boosted Instagram posts, local targeting only | 50 |

## Two things to check before pushing hard
1. **Churn.** If you lose 5–10 subscribers a month, keeping them is as valuable as finding new ones. A pause option for holidays (instead of cancelling) often fixes a lot of this.
2. **Capacity.** How many boxes can 3 people bake and deliver on a Saturday morning? If the ceiling is about 180, you'll hit it after about 40 new subscribers, and growing further would mean more staff, a second bike or a Friday delivery slot.

If you tell me your monthly cancellations and your Saturday capacity, I can help you set a realistic target and timeline.
